CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFQUERYPARAM

NEW IN KOLDFUSION 4.5

CFQUERYPARAM goes inside a CFQUERY wherever a value would appear in the SQL. It checks the value against the SQL type you name and only then hands it to the driver, so a stray quote or a sneaky "; DELETE FROM Employees" never becomes part of the statement.

Category

Database manipulation

Syntax

<CFQUERYPARAM VALUE="parameter_value"
    CFSQLTYPE="parameter_type"
    MAXLENGTH="maximum_length"
    SCALE="decimal_places"
    NULL="Yes/No">

Attributes

VALUE
Required. The value to bind. Usually an expression such as #Form.Emp_ID#.
CFSQLTYPE
Optional, default "CF_SQL_CHAR". The SQL type of the value: CF_SQL_BIGINT, CF_SQL_BIT, CF_SQL_CHAR, CF_SQL_DATE, CF_SQL_DECIMAL, CF_SQL_DOUBLE, CF_SQL_FLOAT, CF_SQL_IDSTAMP, CF_SQL_INTEGER, CF_SQL_LONGVARCHAR, CF_SQL_MONEY, CF_SQL_MONEY4, CF_SQL_NUMERIC, CF_SQL_REAL, CF_SQL_SMALLINT, CF_SQL_TIME, CF_SQL_TIMESTAMP, CF_SQL_TINYINT or CF_SQL_VARCHAR.
MAXLENGTH
Optional. Maximum length of a string value. A longer value throws a Database exception instead of being truncated.
SCALE
Optional. Number of decimal places for CF_SQL_DECIMAL and CF_SQL_NUMERIC. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
NULL
Optional, default "No". Yes sends SQL NULL and ignores VALUE.
LIST
Optional, default "No". KoldFusion extension: Yes treats VALUE as a list and binds every element, for use inside an IN ( ) clause. Each element is validated separately.
SEPARATOR
Optional, default ",". KoldFusion extension: the list delimiter used when LIST="Yes".

Usage

Values are checked before anything reaches the data source:

  • Integer types (CF_SQL_INTEGER, CF_SQL_SMALLINT, CF_SQL_TINYINT, CF_SQL_BIGINT) accept whole numbers only.
  • The other numeric types (DECIMAL, NUMERIC, FLOAT, DOUBLE, REAL, MONEY) accept any number.
  • CF_SQL_BIT accepts Yes/No, True/False or a number and sends 1 or 0.
  • CF_SQL_DATE, CF_SQL_TIME and CF_SQL_TIMESTAMP accept anything IsDate likes and send an ODBC date literal.
  • Everything else is treated as text; single quotes are doubled for you.

A value that fails the check throws an exception of type Database ("Invalid data ... for CFSQLTYPE ..."), which you can catch with CFTRY/CFCATCH. Using the tag outside a CFQUERY is a Template error.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Try ?Dept=Marketing&MinID=7 or ?MinID=abc --->
<CFPARAM NAME="URL.Dept" DEFAULT="Engineering">
<CFPARAM NAME="URL.MinID" DEFAULT="10">
<CFTRY>
  <CFQUERY NAME="GetStaff" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
  SELECT Emp_ID, FirstName, LastName
  FROM Employees
  WHERE Department = <CFQUERYPARAM VALUE="#URL.Dept#" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_VARCHAR" MAXLENGTH="35">
    AND Emp_ID >= <CFQUERYPARAM VALUE="#URL.MinID#" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_INTEGER">
  ORDER BY Emp_ID
  </CFQUERY>
  <CFOUTPUT><H3>#HTMLEditFormat(URL.Dept)#, employee ID #HTMLEditFormat(URL.MinID)# and up</H3></CFOUTPUT>
  <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
  <TR><TH>ID</TH><TH>Name</TH></TR>
  <CFOUTPUT QUERY="GetStaff">
  <TR><TD>#Emp_ID#</TD><TD>#FirstName# #LastName#</TD></TR>
  </CFOUTPUT>
  </TABLE>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Database">
    <CFOUTPUT><P><B>Rejected:</B> #CFCATCH.Message#</P></CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>

<!--- A hostile value never reaches the database --->
<CFTRY>
  <CFQUERY NAME="Sneaky" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
  SELECT * FROM Employees
  WHERE Emp_ID = <CFQUERYPARAM VALUE="3; DELETE FROM Employees" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_INTEGER">
  </CFQUERY>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Database">
    <CFOUTPUT><P><B>Also rejected:</B> #CFCATCH.Message#</P></CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
